topics.title: U.S. marks 25 years since 9/11
topics.summary: Ceremonies across New York, the Pentagon, Pennsylvania, and other communities marked 25 years since the September 11 attacks, with new attention to first responders and later health impacts.
topics.discussionPrompt: How would the studio mark a big anniversary in a way that feels respectful but still personal?

topics.title: Markets rebound as oil cools
topics.summary: U.S. stocks recovered some weekly losses Friday as oil prices slipped and inflation data landed close to expectations, though major indexes still ended the week lower.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the mood suddenly improves after a rough week, who trusts the bounce and who keeps checking the numbers?

topics.title: Cyclospora lettuce outbreak ends
topics.summary: U.S. health officials declared a record cyclospora outbreak over after nearly 13,000 illnesses, while investigators still work to pinpoint how contaminated iceberg lettuce entered the supply chain.
topics.discussionPrompt: If one ingredient caused months of chaos, who in the studio would become the unofficial food-safety inspector?

topics.title: Ebola spreads in Congo
topics.summary: Congo’s Ebola outbreak reached a seventh province, raising concern about travel links, strained health systems, and the need to expand vaccination and clinical trials.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a health warning is serious but far away, how does the studio decide what deserves attention without spiraling?

topics.title: AI safety debate grows louder
topics.summary: Fresh warnings about advanced AI risks pushed lawmakers, experts, and editorial boards to call for stronger oversight, international cooperation, and clearer guardrails.
topics.discussionPrompt: Who in the studio thinks AI needs strict rules, and who thinks everyone is overreacting until something actually breaks?

topics.title: Kyiv pauses for daily silence
topics.summary: AP photos showed Kyiv residents stopping at 9 a.m. for Ukraine’s daily minute of silence, a ritual that has become part of public life since 2022.
topics.discussionPrompt: What tiny daily ritual could make the studio feel more grounded, even when everybody is busy?

topics.title: Hong Kong activists sentenced
topics.summary: A Hong Kong court sentenced three former Tiananmen vigil organizers to prison terms, renewing debate over civic freedoms and Beijing’s national security crackdown.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a tradition becomes politically risky, who keeps showing up and who argues for finding a quieter way?

topics.title: Lettuce prices fall sharply
topics.summary: U.S. lettuce prices dropped after the outbreak hurt demand for leafy greens, even as energy, trade tensions, and other costs kept wider inflation worries alive.
topics.discussionPrompt: What would happen if one cheap menu item suddenly became the studio’s most controversial budget topic?

topics.title: Bayeux Tapestry draws crowds
topics.summary: The British Museum opened its Bayeux Tapestry exhibition to major public interest, turning a nearly thousand-year-old artwork into one of the week’s cultural draws.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the studio made a giant tapestry of its own history, what ridiculous scene absolutely has to be included?

topics.title: Genetic genealogy helps identify remains
topics.summary: CBC reported on a New York lab using genetic genealogy to help identify 9/11 victims’ remains, offering families new answers decades later.
topics.discussionPrompt: When technology finally answers an old question, who finds that comforting and who finds it complicated?
